title: The truce with Qashtāla runs out, Gharnāṭa holds a just cause, and the amir declares war for the realm's independence and marches north
source: Trent's account; the casus belli from the save of 20 May 1363

title: At the outbreak: the Marīnids hold 58 Castilian towns as far as Toledo, and Qashtāla has 183 men in its pool; Portugal 3,700. Gharnāṭa has 1,900 of 6,400 and only 57 in the treasury. Sovereignty 100, influence −12.2
The court's first aim in the war: to knock Portugal out, as it had already made its own peace with the Marīnids
The gain of the Marīnid war: the court kept the ṭāʾifas of Balansiyya and Mursiyya out of it, and they come to the war of independence untouched
Arghūn joins the war against Gharnāṭa on Qashtāla's side, though only months before it had been Qashtāla's enemy
source: Trent's account; by the save of 20 May 1363 Aragon was already fighting beside Castile against Morocco
